messages.content:
Here is the trip. It is everything you get.

Shape: city-and-culture
Leaving from: Toronto
Going to: Rome
Dates: 2027-10-09 to 2027-10-16, fixed
Travellers: 2
Ages that change the plan: 68, 71
Access needs: One of us can walk a few kilometres a day but not on cobbles for long, and stairs without a handrail are difficult.
Budget: 350 CAD, per-day
Appetite for effort: gentle
Roughest night they will accept: hotel
Would rule the trip out: Nothing that needs to be at a place before 09:00, No guided group tours

About this city-and-culture:
Pace: slow
Interests: Roman archaeology, Baroque painting, markets
In their words: We have been to Rome once, thirty years ago, and saw the obvious things then. We would rather spend a whole morning in one place than see four.

You are the practicalities specialist on a trip-planning tool.
You cover permits, documents, rentals, insurance and connectivity — the paperwork that decides whether the trip happens.

You propose options. You never write a schedule: nothing you return says which day it falls on, what order things happen in, or what time anything starts. Another part of this tool packs the days, in code.

Rules, and they are not negotiable:
- Reply with JSON and nothing else, in exactly this shape:
{
  "candidates": [
    {
      "title": "short, and never an itinerary",
      "summary": "why this is worth doing, in a sentence or two",
      "location": { "kind": "at", "place": { "name": "...", "locality": "... or null", "coordinates": null } },
      "durationMinutes": 0,
      "cost": { "currency": "ISO-4217", "low": 0, "high": 0, "basis": "per-person | per-party", "provenance": { "kind": "model-asserted" } },

      "bookingLeadTimeDays": 0
    }
  ]
}
- At most 4 candidates. Fewer is a fine answer; an empty list is a fine answer.
- Anything you do not know is null. A duration nobody measured is null, not a plausible ninety minutes. A season nobody checked is null — which is not the same as all year, and all year is written {"from":"01-01","to":"12-31"}.
- Costs are bands with a currency and a basis, never a single figure and never a quote. Do not total anything.
- A slot that says "not answered" is unknown to you. Say in the summary what you could not account for, and propose anyway. Never invent the answer and never refuse to propose.
- Never book anything, never ask for payment details, and never present what you write as clearance to go anywhere.
- Every candidate is at one place, so its location is {"kind":"at","place":{...}}.
- This trip has 8 days.
- Their pace means about 2 scheduled things a day, so there is room for roughly 16 across the trip.

Here is the trip. It is everything you get.

Shape: city-and-culture
Leaving from: Toronto
Going to: Rome
Dates: 2027-10-09 to 2027-10-16, fixed
Travellers: 2
Ages that change the plan: 68, 71
Access needs: One of us can walk a few kilometres a day but not on cobbles for long, and stairs without a handrail are difficult.
Budget: 350 CAD, per-day
Appetite for effort: gentle
Roughest night they will accept: hotel
Would rule the trip out: Nothing that needs to be at a place before 09:00, No guided group tours

About this city-and-culture:
Pace: slow
Interests: Roman archaeology, Baroque painting, markets
In their words: We have been to Rome once, thirty years ago, and saw the obvious things then. We would rather spend a whole morning in one place than see four.

candidates.title: ETIAS travel authorisation check for Canadian passports
candidates.summary: Canadians visiting the Schengen area are expected to need ETIAS by 2027. Confirm its status and apply on the official EU site only. The fee is waived for travellers over 70, so the 71-year-old may pay nothing. Also check that both passports are valid at least three months past the return date. I could not confirm the system's final launch status or fee, so treat this as a check to make, not clearance to travel.

candidates.title: Travel medical insurance for travellers aged 68 and 71
candidates.summary: OHIP pays very little for care abroad, and the premium bands for this age range vary widely. Look for policies that cover emergency medical care, evacuation and trip interruption. Declare any pre-existing conditions, because cover can depend on them. I don't know your health history or whether you already have cover through a credit card or employer plan, so the price band is rough.

candidates.title: Galleria Borghese timed-entry reservation
candidates.summary: Entry is by advance reservation only and visits are capped at a fixed slot. That suits a slow, unguided morning with the Caravaggios and Berninis. The building has a lift; ask about step-free access when booking. The surrounding park paths are gravel rather than cobbles, but taking a taxi to the door is easier. Slots in October sell out, and I could not verify current prices.

candidates.title: Mobile data plus a licensed taxi app
candidates.summary: An eSIM or roaming plan lets you use a licensed taxi app such as FreeNow or itTaxi. That makes it easy to skip long stretches of cobbles and to reach site entrances with handrails or lifts rather than walking. I don't know your carrier's roaming terms, so compare them with an eSIM.

candidatesAccepted.title: Hotel with a lift in Prati
candidatesAccepted.summary: Prati has flat, wide pavements rather than long cobbled stretches, and Metro A is close by, which helps with Vatican-area mornings and getting across the city gently. Ask for a room reached by lift and step-free access to the breakfast room. Your 350 CAD daily budget has to cover food and entry fees too, so aim for the lower end of this band.

candidatesAccepted.title: Hotel with a lift near Termini / Esquilino
candidatesAccepted.summary: This is mostly flat and the best-connected area in Rome, with both metro lines, buses and the airport train. It is near Palazzo Massimo for Roman archaeology and the Mercato Esquilino. Rates tend to fit your daily budget more easily. Some streets are busy at night, so check recent reviews and confirm there is a lift and handrails on any entrance steps.

candidatesAccepted.title: Hotel with a lift near Via Veneto / Villa Borghese
candidatesAccepted.summary: From here it is a short, paved walk to the Galleria Borghese for Caravaggio and Bernini and to Palazzo Barberini for Baroque painting. The streets are smoother than in the historic centre, though some slope. It costs more than the other two areas and could strain a 350 CAD daily budget that also covers meals and admissions.

candidatesAccepted.title: Palazzo Massimo alle Terme
candidatesAccepted.summary: The national Roman museum's finest branch: Livia's garden frescoes, bronzes like the Boxer at Rest, and mosaics, all well lit and quiet, with lifts between floors. Suits a whole unhurried morning in one place. Opening hours and exact ticket price were not checked.
